Short reflection

What the data supports—and what it cannot prove

The value of this site is not that it produces a single “correct” answer. Its value is that it makes a limited dataset comparable, inspectable, and open to challenge.

What the data supports

The dataset supports descriptive comparisons among the 22 municipalities represented in the file. It can show which municipalities have larger recorded populations, more internet or mobile users, higher population density, larger employment counts, and different education-related measures. From those fields, the site can calculate transparent ratios and gaps and can rank municipalities under an explicit set of user-controlled weights.

That makes the explorer useful for screening. A decision-maker can locate municipalities that combine scale and density, identify places with large differences between population and recorded internet use, compare a shortlist, and test how priorities change when the weights change. The results can guide where to ask better questions or conduct field research first.

What the data cannot prove

The data cannot establish why one municipality differs from another. It cannot show that limited internet use is caused by price, coverage, skills, device access, or preference. It cannot demonstrate unmet willingness to pay, commercial demand, return on investment, project feasibility, or the effect that a new service would have. A high score is not evidence that an intervention will succeed.

The file also lacks a confirmed reference year and complete documentation of its collection and definitions. It contains no measures of household income, service price, network quality, competition, infrastructure capacity, operating cost, capital cost, regulation, or recent change. Because the score is normalized within this small dataset, its values are relative and will change if the inputs, municipalities, or weights change.

My conclusion. I would use the explorer to create a defensible shortlist—not to make a final investment decision. The next step would be to verify the source and date, add market and infrastructure evidence, speak with local stakeholders, and test whether the patterns remain stable under alternative assumptions.
